India's crop looks like 21.0 m bales on the desk model (USDA 23.5) after the driest June–September in its main cotton districts since at least 1991. With the import duty waived to 2026-12-31 India imports about 5.0 m bales (6.2 m if the waiver runs all season) vs USDA's 3.3 m. US cotton to India: 1.0–1.7 m bales against 0.29 m committed, so 0.7–1.4 m of new US sales are still to come. Counting the Brazilian, African and Australian cotton India takes from other buyers, US exports gain about 0.5 m bales in the desk base and 1.2 m in the bearish (big-crop, lower-price) case; in the desk's simulated balance sheet (crop and exports drawn together, India's duty path included) base exports are 12.9 m vs USDA 12.3, ending stocks 2.9 m (bullish 1.5, bearish 4.2; USDA 3.70), and 78% of runs end below USDA. At today's prices more of this demand gets booked. History says the market prices this through what USDA reports by February–March: if USDA's March US stocks/use reaches the desk base, May, May/Jul (-0.46) and Jul/Dec (+6.16) are all cheap (see Price and spreads); Mar/May (-1.46) has stayed a carry outside world-shortage years.
Desk base case 2026/27 ending stocks 2.88 vs USDA 3.70 (stocks/use 20.2% vs 27.0%); bearish 4.25, bullish 1.52.

May is 82.91. Simulating every combination of crop, exports, India's duty path and historical fit, May averages 92 in February–March (65–141, 10th–90th percentile), with a 62% chance it trades 90 or higher by mid-March and 39% that it trades 78 or lower first. Merchants' shorts are 46% of world exports, the most at this time of year since 2010/11; in heavily hedged seasons May rose 16% on average. Fair value in February–March, when USDA's numbers settle: if USDA's March US stocks/use reaches the desk base (20%), May is worth 86–92, May/Jul -0.0 to +0.6 and Jul/Dec +7 to +9; on USDA's 27.0% they are about 77, -0.6 and +2. Today's prices imply a March number near 24% (May) and 22% (Jul/Dec). Mar/May -1.46 has stayed a carry outside world-shortage years. Open interest has already moved forward: May and Jul hold 119k lots, a record for this date since 2000 (median 33k; 38% of the total vs 22%), so less rolls out of Dec and hedge-lifting as mills fix lands in May and Jul. Downside is limited by who sells: growers are well hedged and can hold cotton in the 55¢ loan, producer fixations are modest and merchants are hedged, so funds are the main seller, against 41k lots mills still have to fix; with a book this size May's worst drop to mid-March has averaged -5% (about 79; worst 72).
